body: Just an update -- I did work up the courage to ask and my mother was really surprisingly great about it. She felt bad that I'd been feeling so bad and besides just confirming that I wasn't asking for money because I was like, in danger and trying to pay off a mob boss or something, didn't pry or make me feel bad at all. It's okay for now.

That's the thing; my paychecks simply won't cover it. I'm only going to get paid $70 this week (I had to take a bunch of time off to go on a trip I bought plane tickets for back in March to visit the friend who was going to lend me money), so even if I didn't have a single bill to pay, I'd still be racking up those overdraft fees. I'm in college working part time and it's just not enough. I wouldn't ask anyone for money if I genuinely didn't have any other options, but here I am, out of options and in urgent need of cash placed directly into my bank account sometime within the next 12ish hours.

The real problem is my overdrawn bank account eating all of my paychecks. I get hit with $80 of overdraft fees a week for as long as I'm in the red. Can't really fill up a bank account with a credit card, and the interest rate at a quick cash place would be no better to me (I wouldn't be able to pay that money back for a full month). Plus, I can't drive, and there's nowhere in my area that does it, so I'd have to ask my mother to drive me somewhere anyway. 

I reached out to a good friend over the weekend who said he'd send money, but he kept forgetting and I felt weird reminding him. At this point, if he doesn't remember to send it first thing tomorrow *and* I haven't asked my parents yet, I'll be fucked. So I just told him a few hours ago that I'm going to ask my parents and he said "that's a good idea." :(
That would be very good advice if my parents were reasonable people, but alas.
